question: In September, the Union Cabinet approved the One Nation, One Poll recommendations proposed by whom among the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ram Nath Kovind**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Union Cabinet approved the **One Nation, One Poll** recommendations proposed by a committee led by former President **Ram Nath Kovind** in September 2023.
 
• This initiative seeks to synchronize the timing of Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections to reduce the frequency of elections and associated costs.
 
• The government formed the committee under Ram Nath Kovind's chairmanship to examine the feasibility of implementing the "One Nation, One Poll" policy.
 
• The proposal aims to enhance administrative efficiency, reduce the burden on security forces, and ensure seamless governance by avoiding frequent imposition of the Model Code of Conduct.
 
• The committee includes legal experts, political leaders, and representatives from various government bodies to ensure the recommendations are comprehensive and inclusive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **One Nation, One Poll:**

 
 
• This concept refers to holding simultaneous elections for the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, and local bodies across the country.
 
• It aims to reduce election-related expenses and frequent disruptions to development activities caused by repeated imposition of the Model Code of Conduct.
 
• The idea was first proposed during the tenure of Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee and has been discussed multiple times in recent years.
 
 
 
• **Committee Formation:**
 
 
• In 2023, the Union Government set up a high-level committee under the chairmanship of Ram Nath Kovind to deliberate on the feasibility of implementing this electoral reform.
 
• The committee includes members from political parties, legal experts, and representatives from the Election Commission of India (ECI).
 
 
 
• **Advantages of One Nation, One Poll:**
 
 
• Reduction in the cost of conducting frequent elections.
 
• Minimization of policy paralysis and disruptions in governance caused by repeated elections.
 
• Streamlining of security personnel deployment and efficient management of resources.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• Constitutional amendments are required to synchronize the terms of various legislative bodies.
 
• Political consensus is necessary to implement the reform successfully.
 
• Logistical challenges such as voter education, preparedness of the Election Commission, and managing simultaneous elections on a large scale.
